llm.summary: The skill largely does what it claims (quant pipeline + optional billing), but there are several inconsistencies and security concerns — most notably a hard-coded billing API key and undocumented external endpoints — that warrant review before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The code implements factor mining, strategy generation, backtesting and evaluation as described. The presence of billing functionality and pricing in SKILL.md is consistent with the included billing.py and skill_with_billing.py. Minor incoherences: SKILL metadata at the top listed 'Homepage: none' while SKILL.md includes a homepage URL; the manifest references a file name btc_predictor_optimized.py that is not present in the provided file contents.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs installation of Python packages and running the included scripts. The runtime code performs network calls to external services: data requests to https://api.hyperliquid.xyz and billing calls to https://skillpay.me. The billing component will POST user_id and attempt charges; this is not expressed as requiring any explicit credentials from the installer (the code contains a hard-coded API key). The skill does not ask to read unrelated system files, but it will transmit user-provided IDs and pipeline data to external endpoints — users should be aware of that external network activity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No elevated install mechanism is included; SKILL.md suggests pip installing common Python libs (lightgbm, pandas, numpy, requests). There are no downloads from unknown URLs or archive extraction instructions in the install spec.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, yet billing.py embeds a long-lived API key (API_KEY) directly in source. Embedding a secret in distributed code is a sensitive practice: if the key is valid it can be abused or indicates secret leakage. Aside from the hard-coded key, the skill does not request unrelated credentials or config paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent/always-on inclusion. It does not modify other skills or system-wide configurations. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not combined with other elevated privileges in this package.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- Network behavior: The skill will make outbound HTTP requests to at least two external services (Hyperliquid for market data and skillpay.me for billing). If you run the skill, data (including any user_id you pass) will be sent to those endpoints.
- Hard-coded secret: billing.py contains a visible API key. Treat this as a red flag — ask the author why the key is embedded, and request that billing credentials be moved to environment variables or platform secret storage. If you plan to use billing, rotate the key and use a dedicated credential.
- Verify endpoints and ownership: skillpay.me and api.hyperliquid.xyz are third-party endpoints. Confirm they are legitimate, that you trust them, and that the skill's homepage/author information matches those services. The registry metadata/homepage in the package is inconsistent; ask the publisher for authoritative contact and hosting info.
- Missing/extra files: The manifest references btc_predictor_optimized.py but it isn't included — confirm the complete codebase and intended inputs/outputs before running.
- Billing behavior: The skill will attempt to charge a user_id passed to the script. Consider testing with a sandbox account and monitor network traffic and billing activity.
- Best practice: Prefer not to run with elevated privileges; run the skill in an isolated environment (container/VM) if you want to test. Request the author to remove hard-coded secrets, document the external services, and explain the billing flow. If you cannot verify the billing API and homepage, treat the skill as untrusted.
llm.findings: [hardcoded-api-key] unexpected: billing.py contains a hard-coded API_KEY string (sk_72d...) used to call https://skillpay.me. While a billing integration needs an API key conceptually, embedding a secret in published source is insecure and unexpected; a properly designed skill would read such keys from protected environment variables or platform-managed secret storage.
